utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Court's permission, I'll continue the examination of B-024?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. According to my calculation, you've had about two hours so far, a bit less. So if you could be as expeditious as possible so that we can make sure that we get the cross-examination in and, if possible, deal with the other witness today. We will sit a bit later, but not beyond 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness B-024, as you're called here, you are, of course, under a declaration, the same declaration that you gave before. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, we interrupted your testimony the week before last. You were describing your relation between the Serb MUP and the RS MUP. Is there anything we neglected or anything that you wish to add to that relationship that we did not get to before we interrupted your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I did work until the 20th of April, 1992 in MUP, and I know that up until then relationships were quite correct and proper. After that, I didn't work in the Ministry of the Interior any more, so I really can't talk about the specifics of the relationships that prevailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the course of this trial, a video was played. It was Prosecution Exhibit 390, tab 18. It was a videotape of a Red Berets celebration at Kula camp. Did you have an opportunity or by chance see that video as it was broadcast in the proceedings of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was played on all sorts of television networks very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise somebody in that video as somebody who was present in Zvornik during the course of the takeover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of the well-known people from the footage, there was only Lukovic, Legija. And as far as I know, he was captured before the Serb forces took Zvornik. He was captured by the Territorial Defence, that is to say, the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from him and the obviously well-known people, was there another person who you recognised as being present in -- that you recognised from that video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of those present, there was just this other man, the one that gave his name to the centre, and that is Radislav Kostic. And the centre is named after him. As to the rest, during the takeover of Zvornik, I don't remember that anybody else was there of those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I might just correct for the record. It was tab 1 of Prosecution Exhibit 390.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'd just ask you to briefly comment. Are you aware of a person by the name of Captain Dragan, and what, if any, involvement did he have in the events that took place in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I've forgot. Yes, of course, I do know Captain Dragan, and I do know that one of his units was in Zvornik with him and he was there for about 30 days. They were put up at the hotel called Vidikovac near Zvornik in a place called Divic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you approximate for us the period of time that Captain Dragan was in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I remember, it may have been May or June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever have a conversation with Mr. Grujic regarding Captain Dragan's presence in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have a conversation with him. And Captain Dragan had some programmes broadcast over the local radio station. This was common knowledge. Everybody knew that he was there in Zvornik with part of his unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to now draw your attention to Kulagrad. Can you describe what, if any, involvement or what, if any, Serb forces were involved in the fighting at Kulagrad towards the middle of April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that. And it was common knowledge. I think the unit was the 72nd Parachute Unit under the command of the then-Lieutenant Colonel Mr. Stupar, which took part in taking control of Kulagrad sometime towards the end of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any other units involved besides that particular one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, all the rest were volunteer units and Territorial Defence of Zvornik. I don't know that there were any other units present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you aware of any of the events that took place in Celopek around this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what events you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Events in the -- the cultural centre at Celopek.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, like most of the inhabitants of Zvornik, I too heard about what was going on in Celopek through the stories told around town and the information media started writing about this abroad too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: A witness has mentioned in detail about what happened in Celopek. Can I just ask you to summarise the types or kinds of crimes or events you heard were occurring in Celopek. Just perhaps list them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was generally known that a group of men from Divic were being incarcerated in Celopek. And according to the stories that went round town and later on published in the information media, and there was also court proceedings in Yugoslavia against the perpetrators, that these people were subjected to terrible torture, killings, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The media accounts, were they contemporaneous -- did they appear in the summer of 1992 or did they appear sometime later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They appeared later, several months later, and they appeared abroad. News of that appeared abroad. And then it was the Yugoslav papers such as Vreme that started writing about it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to now draw your attention to the fighting around the area of Divic. What, if any, JNA participation are you aware of in the fighting around Divic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I don't know that the JNA took part in the attack on Divic. What I do know is that same team which took control of Kulagrad, on that same day crossed over and attacked Divic as an inhabited, built-up area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the attack on Divic, was there any artillery fire from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the attack on Divic, I heard some shooting from all sides. And as far as I know, I don't know if it was artillery fire but there was shooting from the hydroelectric powerplant in Mali Zvornik, and that's in Serbia. Because, in fact, it's a settlement which is several hundred metres away from the hydroelectric powerplant, about 100 metres away, in fact. And this as a strategic target was an interesting one, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know who was responsible for the fire coming from Mali Zvornik, the Serbian side of the border?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. But unequivocally the fire was opened from the Serbia side. But I wasn't there, so I don't know who opened fire first, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to events at the Karakaj Technical School. Are you aware of the events leading up to and the events which occurred at the Karakaj Technical School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is this, that several villages which were loyal to the Serbian authorities surrendered to those authorities and that their transport was organised from a place called Bijeli Potok. But before that, the men were separated from the women and children, and the women and children were taken off in the direction of Kalesija, up until a place called Memelic [phoen], and the men were incarcerated in the technical school in Karakaj. And very soon after that, rumours began to go round Zvornik that they were actually killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you to describe in a little greater detail, when you said villages loyal to Serb authorities. What was the ethnic make-up of these villages that you're saying were loyal to Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those villages were ethnically pure and inhabited by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, when you say "loyal to Serb authorities," is that to say that they observed or subjected themselves to the new temporary government, Serb government, that you described earlier in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, there were no military events in those villages from the time that Serb -- the Serbs took control of Zvornik until they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the fact that there were no military events in these villages, was that something only you and a few people knew or was that something widely known by the people present in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was common knowledge in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Returning to Karakaj Technical School, and putting rumour aside, did you yourself ever go to the area or to the school itself during the time that these men were held at that school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day the people were brought there, I did go over there to take two men there which had been appointed by the headquarters, that is to say, the headquarters had sent them up for an exchange, a so-called exchange. I was taking them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to secure the release of a former colleague of yours who had been detained at the Karakaj school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a written order from the TO commander. I didn't actually enter the school building, but I handed this over to the people that stood guard in front of the school, and they took out my former colleague, along with another man who was the president of the SDA in Djulici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what it was or what your observations were about the conditions at the school at the time that you were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I conveyed that to the TO commander. The conditions were catastrophic. It was June. It was extremely hot. And you could see the humidity coming out of the room as they opened the door to let the people out. You could see that it was stifling inside and that it was all steamed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from that particular occasion, did you ever return to the school while men were being detained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of General Subotic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to 1995, did you have a conversation with General Subotic that related to the events or the people that had been detained in Karakaj Technical School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never had a conversation with General Subotic about that subject. I received information from a colleague, however, who was in the Crisis Staff, that he had discussed those events with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did your colleague describe to you as the conversation he had with General Subotic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I came to see him privately, to have a cup of coffee with him, and I just happened to come upon General Subotic there. We didn't discuss any vital subjects. It was just a normal chitchat, private chitchat. And when he left, the man told me that General Subotic had the assignment given to him by the government at Pale to do everything in his power to see that the mass graves around the municipality and Republika Srpska be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you learn the location to where the mass graves were to be moved to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't learn of the location, but later on talking to a policeman -- as I say, later on he explained to me that they provided security for very strange transport and that during the night a road was shut off to traffic from Zvornik towards Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Chamber's benefit where Crni Vrh is in comparison to the centre of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Crni Vrh is approximately 15 to 20 kilometres -- 15 kilometres on the road to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to the issue of pensions. And my question to you is: Can you describe what you know about whether pensions were paid to non-Serbs after the takeover of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that pensions were not paid to the non-Serb inhabitants after the 9th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all the lists of salaries and pensions had to go to the provisional -- the temporary government to be authorised and certified. And I know that the Muslims on those lists did not get the go-ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to take a look at this exhibit. It's a multi-page exhibit. But if I could draw your attention to the -- the piece of -- the document with "InvestBanka" on the top right-hand corner. I believe it's the exhibit you're looking at now. And if I could ask you to read the first full paragraph of that document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What it says here: "We ask you to, for the purpose of payments for April to the pensioners of Serb ethnicity who received their pensions though InvestBank in Zvornik, allocate the amount of," and then there's a large amount. It stresses here that the pensioners were of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During your contacts with the Crisis Staff, did you ever see a similar document authorising the payment of pensions to people of non-Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you did see similar documents authorising the payment of pensions to people of ethnicity other than Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw there was a misunderstanding. I saw documents in which the government, the provisional government, prohibited the payment to workers, payment of sums of money to workers who were non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit. Thank you to the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I now draw your attention to Kozluk. Are you aware of the -- an occasion in which nearly the entire population of that village left Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That was at the beginning of the war, and I was still the commander, the chief of the station. And we did visit Kozluk, which was preparing for people to leave it. Everybody was on tractors and trucks and the Gornji Sepak village, the Muslim village, joined in. I would say there were roughly six or seven thousand people there, and I was a member of the delegation, where the Muftija and Orthodox church leader was there and we tried to convince those people not to leave Kozluk. And at that time we succeeded and they did return to their homes. We made lists of their requirements and assisted them as far as we were able to at that particular point in time. And they did stay on living in Kozluk for several months after that, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe what events transpired between this event you're talking about and the period of time or the day when they eventually did leave en masse.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I know is this: I had telephone conversations with some members from Kozluk, although I wasn't in the Crisis Staff or the police any more. And they shade they had been ordered sometime at the beginning of July 1992, I think it was, and that they had been pulled out of Kozluk. They were simply told that that was the decision that had been reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What, if any, involvement did a person by the name of Peja have in this event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that Peja was Arkan's deputy throughout Arkan's operation -- the operations of Arkan's unit in Zvornik. Now, if you are referring to Peja's part in pulling people out of Kozluk, I don't think he was in Kozluk at that time because they left Zvornik between the 15th and 20th of April and the unit was no longer in Zvornik and the surrounding territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now ask you to take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 14. It is a receipt. I'm going to ask you: Do you recognise what's described in this receipt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a receipt for the provisional government of the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik for services of transport. And then it gives the locations, Zvornik-Kozluk-Gornji Sepak, Petkovci-Kiseljak, Zvornik-Bijeljina-Batkovic, Zvornik-Kozluk, Orahovac, Karakaj, et cetera. And then the invoices, which were paid by the municipality to the transport company, Drinatrans - that was its name - from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to an entry of the 15th of July, 1992. And the route that is described as Zvornik-Bijeljina-Batkovic. And it says, "Four vehicles were used to transport 600 prisoners." Can you see that entry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. That was on the 15th of July, 1992. Zvornik-Bijeljina-Batkovic was the route, four buses, 600 it says here, transport for detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know where those detainees specifically were transported to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. All I can say is to comment on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to now draw your attention to what, if any, damage was done to the mosques in the municipality of Zvornik. And my first question to you is: During the actual takeover of Zvornik, were any of the mosques destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, up until the 20th of April I was there, not a single mosque in the Zvornik municipality had been destroyed. But as a citizen of Zvornik who worked there and resided there throughout, I do know that all the mosques in Zvornik and the surrounding parts under the control of the authorities, controlled by the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik, in some time -- at some time in 1992 were for the most part either destroyed or damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe what you know about the circumstances surrounding the destruction of these mosques.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as a citizen myself, all I could notice was that I went by several days later and saw that a mine -- a mosque in Zvornik had been mined, blown up, and that the glass windowpanes had been shattered on some of the surrounding buildings. That's all I can tell you about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the destruction of the mosque, was it some -- was it due to spontaneous retaliation by citizens or was it organised by the authorities in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any evidence of it being organised, but the only thing I can say as an individual, as my opinion, it was in reaction to the war and the events that were going on in Zvornik and throughout Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could go into closed session just for my second-to-last question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay. We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And sir, my final question to you is: Have any promises been made to you in exchange for your testimony before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. B-024, you said that the attack on Zvornik took place on the 8th of April, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, with precision, as somehow I was not quite able to follow, which units took part in that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were units of the Territorial Defence of Zvornik, assisted by volunteers from various parts. I don't really know who they were. They were coming from all over. And about 20 to 30 members of Arkan's unit, under the command of his deputy at the time, Pejic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So no JNA units took part in that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I said at the beginning, that I was not aware of any JNA units taking part in the attack on Zvornik on the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're not aware of the presence of any police unit, for instance, from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no presence of the police from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in those conflicts, there were units of the Zvornik Territorial Defence participating and volunteers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this unit of Arkan's, the Serbian Volunteer Guard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did the Muslim forces put up any resistance and what kind? What did that conflict look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was not involved at the front line because I was injured. I was at headquarters. But I do know that the first conflict in Zvornik resulted in the withdrawal of Serbs from Zvornik a month prior to the outbreak of the conflict because of the tension, so there were very few Serbs sleeping in Zvornik, so that Zvornik was more or less ethnically pure that is, there were only Muslims there. And then they distributed what weapons were left in the SUP for the reserve force and they had their own Territorial Defence. The conflict didn't last long. One could hear the shooting in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Before you tell me how long the conflict lasted, but on the basis of your own knowledge - you were in Zvornik at the time - the Muslim forces, that is, the Territorial Defence, and the police, the Muslim part of the Zvornik SUP held the whole of Zvornik under control, whereas the Serbs had fled Zvornik in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you have any idea as to where the most significant points were at which Muslim forces were concentrated prior to the outbreak of the conflict in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have an idea, in view of the job I did. They were at Kulagrad, on the surrounding hills around Zvornik, and at the very entrance to Zvornik at Vidakova Njiva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So would it be right to say that apart from the Serbian part, that is, where the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik had been formed in a Serbian settlement, the whole of Zvornik had been captured by Muslim forces and under their control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, prior to the outbreak of the conflict. That is true. The whole of the town of Zvornik was held by Muslim forces for several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you have any idea of the strength of those Muslim forces that held Zvornik at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to put it, but our estimate was that the forces were significant. They were considerable. Because we had some information as to the arming of the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more precise about that? How big?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that from the Zvornik SUP, about 500 pieces of weapons had been distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When Serbs took Karakaj and left Zvornik, they distributed about 500 long barrels to the reserve force of their police, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the reserve force. And what makes it worse is to the criminals that they rounded up in the street and distributed weapons to them, and that is what frightened the Serbs and prompted them to leave Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And those criminals, when they were armed in Zvornik, what were they doing in Zvornik to frighten the Serbs and prompt them to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was about two or three days prior to the conflict. They put on uniforms, and they were admitted overnight to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But what were they doing in the streets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They started checking entry and exit into and from Zvornik and checking and questioning citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean "questioning citizens and controlling them"? Did they arrest people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that there were any arrests, but they simply took over the job that was done by the regular police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Apart from those 500 reserve members of the police, how many members of the Territorial Defence did they have organised in Zvornik or the units known as the Green Berets and the Patriotic League? I assume you're aware of those units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew and all of us in the staff knew that already in October 1991, in the village of Godus, the Patriotic League had been formed and they had certain quantities of weapons. We also knew that at Kula a unit of theirs was stationed and somebody called Captain Hajro was with them, who had deserted the Yugoslav People's Army. But I don't know of how strong they were. And as we were in the minority in Zvornik, I assume they were quite numerous, because according to the 1991 census 70 per cent of the population of Zvornik were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't have an idea of the strength of the -- their Territorial Defence that held Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you ask me to give you a number, I can't give you a number, but it was significant and it could be measured in several thousand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think your explanation is quite sufficient. Could you tell me, please, how long that battle for Zvornik lasted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The actual attack on Zvornik lasted from about 4.00 a.m. until 8.00 a.m., so about four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since all of you knew about these things, because you said several times during your testimony Zvornik is a small town, everyone knows everyone else and everyone knows what's going on, tell me, how many Serb fighters were killed in the battle for Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean throughout the war or during that first day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During the fighting, the battle, how many Serb fighters were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war from 1992 to 1995, about 1.000 Serb combatants were killed in Zvornik in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, that day when the conflict broke out, the battle for Zvornik, that was held by Muslim forces as you described, how many Serb fighters were killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have precise records, but I think the Serbs had three or four dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many Muslim combatants were killed, members of their armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what the civil defence said later on, I think about 20 persons were buried, whose bodies were found there after the battle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So we are talking about the 8th of April, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please: Immediately after the expulsion of the Muslim forces from Zvornik, they blocked Zvornik, the Serb forces captured Zvornik, these others withdrew. Then the municipal leadership, did it take steps to prevent looting, rioting, and to restore the situation to normal in town, to resume production, and generally to normalise life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were attempts by the Crisis Staff at the time. They did everything they could to bring life back to normal. However, as the war operations continued and there were more and more dead, it was more and more difficult to keep things under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were measures taken to prevent looting, violence, and other illegal acts, and did the municipal authorities take care of these things or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was saying, there were attempts to do something as far as that was possible; however, shortly forces organised themselves that were stronger than the local police and the local TO, so that as far as I know it was not possible to keep things really properly under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the events that you spoke about a moment ago, saying that things got out of hand and there were various groups and later on you speak of the destruction of mosques and so on, so this was something that wasn't planned or organised but simply the consequence of the general chaos that set in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that things were not developing in the direction that I thought the struggle of the Serb people would take for equality, that the things were getting out of control. I abandoned the staff and the police, but I do know that the president of the Crisis Staff was slapped around several times by various paramilitaries, that he was several times taken to be executed, and that it is really hard to establish who had control in Zvornik in the months of May, June, and July until that well-known operation of arrest of paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So what you just said a moment ago, towards the end of your examination-in-chief, this was not an organised destruction of mosques but a reaction to wartime events by various groups that were present there at the time, armed citizens and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that as an individual, I did not attend any meeting at which there was discussion of any plans or agreements to destroy any places of worship. But also as a human being, I must say that all the Muslim religious buildings were destroyed in 1992 when the town was under Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And across the way in Mali Zvornik, in which as you also know there were some Muslims living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know that in Zvornik municipality there is an ethnic group of Muslims accounting for, I think, about 20 per cent of the population of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in the territory of Serbia, in Mali Zvornik municipality, across the Drina, there is a mosque too. Yes, there is a mosque there, which was never damaged.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that it was never damaged. I know that the police guarded it at the beginning of the conflict, when the situation was most critical.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the conflict it was so, but also later on no one touched the mosque, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after Zvornik was captured, as we described a moment ago, were there arrests of individual members of these Muslim paramilitary formations, their taking into custody and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know as a citizen, I think not. Most of their military formations withdrew after the Serbs entered Zvornik. For a time, they were at Kula. And after Kula was captured, some went towards Tuzla and others towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. When the Crisis Staff was formed, I gathered from what you were saying that the Crisis Staff was formed, your Crisis Staff in Zvornik - I'm talking about that one - for -- in order to protect the Serb people from possible attacks by Muslim forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And was there ever any discussion within that Crisis Staff that Muslim villages needed to be attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in my testimony, that I was never present at any meeting of the Crisis Staff at which it was said that a single Muslim should be killed or a Muslim village attacked or cleansed. All we spoke about was about the protection of the Serbs in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can we infer from that that, for instance, the attack on the village known as Kulagrad was carried out exclusively because it was a stronghold of Muslim forces in the immediate vicinity of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who are in Zvornik and who are familiar with the geography of Zvornik, Kulagrad is actually a component part of Zvornik, it is a height close to Zvornik which dominates over Zvornik. And it is not possible to organise life normally in Zvornik under wartime conditions if one doesn't have control of Kulagrad as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Dr. Muhamed Jelkic, who is a Muslim, was he a member of some particular body in Zvornik? You mention him on page 9 of this tape 6 to 9 in your statement, in what I got as your transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Muhamed Jelkic was a member of the Crisis Staff and a member of the provisional government in the Municipality of Zvornik for a while at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did he try and the very fact that he was a member of the Crisis Staff and this provisional government, was that an expression of the efforts made to normalise inter-ethnic relations and for the situation to calm down, to make it possible for those who had fled town, civilians, to come back, things like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely what the original idea was, and Muhamed Jelkic had very good intentions and was very honest. But now that I've mentioned the man here, I have to say that I did talk to him and he told me rather soon that all of this was assuming different proportions and that he felt as if he were a detainee, being a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how many Muslims stayed in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who happened to be there. I mean, those who had not fled, simply were in Zvornik. And I know that over the local radio calls were issued to the population to the return to their workplaces and also to protect their property. And I think that in the beginning of May in Zvornik there were quite a few Muslims who had returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody mistreat them there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I had no such information. But later on, when I talked to these people, I realised that there were such cases as well. But that is what I learned subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But when one bears in mind the fact that the Muslim population was called upon over the radio to return, to continue working, et cetera, all of that was within the efforts to normalise the situation in Zvornik; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can one say, then, at all that somebody was carrying out some kind of ethnic cleansing there if at the same time everybody is being called upon to return and to have the situation normalised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that this cannot be explained in one sentence only. The original idea was -- the original idea that we believed in was that people should come back and the situation should go back to normal. However, as the war progressed, more and more people were losing their lives and paramilitary formations were getting stronger and stronger. Quite simply there was no control any longer and it wasn't safe for these people to stay in Zvornik after their return.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please explain this to me, because I really am not aware of the situation in Zvornik itself. All these formations, didn't they -- I mean, weren't they rather quickly put under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska somehow, or were there formations that were formations of the Army of Republika Srpska but that did not accept the command of the Army of Republika Srpska? What was the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the key question. Formally, perhaps, but if you look at the substance -- I mean, my own assessment is and most people from Zvornik will tell you that from the beginning of May until July practically there was no government and authority there. It is practically the paramilitaries that ruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to speak up a little bit, please, when you answer your questions, because I find it difficult to understand what you're saying, but I have understood what you've said so far. Tell me, since you mentioned this meeting between Stevo Radic - this is on page 13, tape 6 to 9 - you mention the meeting between Stevo Radic and Zuca in the house of Dr. Vidovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: I didn't find this clear, and it was my understanding that you were not present.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that at this meeting they discussed the takeover of power in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The paramilitaries had the objective of taking over power in Zvornik. And I think that they had already made all the necessary assignments, who should take which particular office. They invited Radic to this meeting too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who was Radic, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radic was a member of the Crisis Staff, and he was in charge of the economy in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the man you refer to as Zuca, he's the one who was later arrested and tried?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was arrested and tried before a court of law in Sabac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Sabac is in Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's the man who was killing people at that cultural centre in Celopek; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never present there. I just heard the testimony of witnesses. But I never was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. On page 1, tape 7 to 9 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I -- Your Honour, may I just finish this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to Celopek, they called Radic and they suggested this to him, but he did not accept this. And he was beaten up by them there, Radic was. And then something strange happened. Dr. Vidovic was killed in his apartment in Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, since you referred to the killings of some persons in Djulici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who committed these killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that people were transported to the technical school centre in Karakaj and that they were separated from the women and children, but I personally do not know who ordered these killings and who actually committed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about this technical school in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was there in front, the first day when they were brought there, and it was the police and the TO of the municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Together, the TO and the police of Zvornik held Karakaj together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The school where the people were detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: How did Brano Grujic react? You mention him as president of the municipality at the time. Was he at that time president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Grujic was president of the municipality at the time. Afterwards, when it became clear that these people were missing, in a private conversation a year or two ago I asked him about that particular case and he swore to me that he knew nothing about this and that this was done without his knowledge and that he had no information about this and he did not take part in any of this, neither the ordering of the killing or the killing itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But on the basis of the knowledge you had then, not only on the basis of this conversation you had two or three years ago, the one that you referred to just now, what happened obviously did not happen under the control of the president of the municipality of Zvornik and your Crisis Staff and this provisional government of yours. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, at that time I was not on the Crisis Staff or in the government. At that time, I was director of a company. And I can only say what I heard from people with whom I had contacts. I don't have any reliable or valid information about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But do you have any information about your Crisis Staff and generally speaking the authorities that had been organised there after the takeover of Zvornik? Did they play any role in this, in any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. crime that had been committed there against these detained persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the units of Captain Dragan. A witness here before you said that he came only with two or three men, that he was involved only in the training of the local Territorial Defence. Did you see this unit of his? Did he have a unit or did he not have a unit? I wish we could clarify that. According to the information I have, he did not have a unit at all. He was engaged in training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you can keep your questions short, it will be much easier for the witness to answer. What the accused is putting is that Captain Dragan didn't have a unit and that he came with just a few men. Can you assist us to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is generally known. He came with two or three instructors and he gathered a unit out of the local people that he had taken over from the TO. He was supposed to train them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said on page 3 in this statement of yours that it is well known that the JNA supported the struggle of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to be very specific about this now. This support, is it directly linked to a common value, so to speak, that both had one and the same objective, that is to say, to preserve Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: These Muslim forces, were they hostile towards the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim leadership, did they order the Muslims not to respond to JNA call-ups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is generally known.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this has to do with working for the preservation of Yugoslavia, as concerns the JNA and as concerns the Serb population; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that the key point was the international recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That was the main problem for the army and for the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This was said by Lord Carrington and other national representatives. As you often say here, the way you put it, this is a generally-known thing. But tell me now, please: On page 19, in the 12th paragraph, you refer to a certain Ratko Vidovic, who had been sent from Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which contact this was, but Ratko Vidovic was not sent from anywhere. He was commander and then chief of police in Mali Zvornik throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm glad that we've cleared this up. So he had not been sent by anyone and he did not have any assignments there. He was simply a policeman there in the neighbouring municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before the war and during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He did not hold any other particular office, especially not on the other side of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was just in charge of his own work.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, as regards the municipal leadership of Zvornik, this newly-established government, Crisis Staff, et cetera, who did they report to about their work, the municipal leadership?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the plan, Plan A and Plan B, we belonged to the municipality that was in the B version. We reported to the Crisis Staff, which was then in Sarajevo, the Crisis Staff of the Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to be very specific about this, because slowly we are going to paint an entire picture of all of this. I'm not only referring to your testimony but to others as well. So you directly reported to the Crisis Staff in Sarajevo. You did not go through the Crisis Staff of this Autonomous Region and so on and so forth. You directly reported to Sarajevo, your municipality did; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because at that time, there weren't any Crisis Staffs of autonomous regions. They came into existence only later, just before the war broke out. So practically by then all communications with Sarajevo had been severed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Were you in the Crisis Staff for a while?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that. I was in the Crisis Staff from its establishment until the 12th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you in charge of the Crisis Staff for a while?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never in charge of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 38, in paragraph 11, you say that you had a video cassette on which there is footage from a village which is called Godus, where the Patriotic League had been formed or, rather, this extremist military organisation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. These video materials were also shown on Bosnian television, and now on that particular site there is a monument that was built in memory of this event that took place in October in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many people were there in full combat gear and when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in October 1991. And there was about a company there, about 100 people under full combat gear with radio communications, with all necessary equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At that time, there were no conflicts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the municipality of Zvornik and in all of Bosnia, there were no conflicts at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In all of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were no conflicts at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In October 1991, this Patriotic League, judging by all of this, was a paramilitary formation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, knowledge of this nature, namely, things that had to do with the preparation and arming of these military -- of these Muslim formations, did they affect you? And when I say "did they affect you," I'm not referring to only you yourself but I am referring to you, the people of Zvornik. Did it cause concern among you? Did you start organising yourselves in order to defend yourselves and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I already said this. After having found out about this, we went and asked for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was that the reason why you sought help from Arkan, for instance, the Serb Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not know Arkan. I was not aware of the existence of the Serb Volunteer Guard. But we did address our request for help to Serbia, and afterwards we did get in touch with Arkan too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you said during the examination-in-chief that you took his unit over the Drina and came to Zvornik with them, I'm just interested in one particular piece of information. You saw all of them. You said that there were about 20 of them; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It was about 10 or 12 years ago. But I said it was between 20 or 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's important to establish that because there were witnesses here who said that there were many more of them. And I have information that is similar to what you have said. I have information that there were 24 of them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, they were put up at the hotel in Radanj, which can take a total of 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't only them who were there probably.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So we've managed to clear that point up, that Arkan with 20 men launched an aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, that is something that is being claimed here. And tell me this, please: On page 43, you say that it was rumoured around Zvornik that you in fact brought Arkan into Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm reading all this from your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say that you did not oppose the rumours, you let people think what they wanted, that you were friends, and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, when the war began in Zvornik, it was a good thing for people to think that Arkan was your friend. I never denied it, but actually I saw him in Bijeljina for the first time and heard of his existence only one day previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell me this, please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There was a meeting between Grujic, Radic, Pavlovic in Mali Zvornik, with the Muslim representatives. That's right, isn't it? That's what you say on page 44, I think.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke about that last time. There's a videotape. And I apologise, Your Honours, when I enumerated the names. Stevo Radic did not attend the meeting. It was Mijatovic, Grujic, myself and Stevo Ivanovic on the Serb side. And on the Muslim side there was -- there were their own representatives. And Marko Pavlovic did not attend that particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He did not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But the five of you did. There were the five of you from the top echelons of the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many representatives were there on the Muslim side, of the Muslim authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were also about five of them; it was parity on a parity basis. If there was the mayor on one side, there was the mayor on the other. If there was the chief of police on one side, there was the chief on the other, a parity balance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So people on the Muslim side were the same in rank as the people on your side, the Serb side; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was goal of the meeting? As far as I understand it, the object of the meeting was to reduce tensions generally and to quell the situation and to solve the problems in Zvornik in a peaceful way. Was that the purpose of the meeting, or was there some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have defined the main points of the meeting. Those were the points exactly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me this, please: Why did the meeting not succeed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did reach an agreement. And I would say that the meeting was successful. But two days later it was not successful because we followed the situation, each of us in our own field, and two days later another meeting was organised, because among others we had decided to maintain constant communication and we decided to send the president of the then-municipality, the executive board, Mr. Mijatovic and Ivanovic to the meeting, and they also sent their president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was Mijatovic, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mijatovic was in the B version that we had set up before the war parallelly with the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me this now, please: You say in referring to Pavlovic that he had links with politicians and generals. Could you tell us with which politicians and which generals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he had good relationships with the army. As to the politicians, I really don't know what his relationships with them were. But I do know that he did have relationships with Mr. Panic. I think he was at the time the head of the army, of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, from the statement -- or rather, your live testimony here, you said that he had some relations with the commander of the Tuzla Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that he spent some time in Tuzla often. I know that he was in company with General Savo Jankovic, he was the commander of the Tuzla Corps at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And your area of responsibility was at the Tuzla Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the JNA division, we came under the Tuzla Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And Pavlovic was commander of the Territorial Defence of your locality; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I spoke about the contacts that he had prior to the conflict, while he was not commander of the TO yet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not hear the question of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you then appointed him TO commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then he maintained intensive contacts, as far as I was able to understand. Was it logical that in the area of responsibility of the JNA corps the command of the Territorial Defence of one -- a particular place in the area of responsibility should have contacts with the command of the corresponding units of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that you had very bad relations with Pavlovic, you were on bad terms with him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on good terms with him until the 10th of 15th of April. After that, it's not that our relations were bad, but we had very -- we had contact on very rare occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to clear that up, because on page 49 I saw that you said that you were on bad terms with him. But I assume that you didn't say that in that way specifically. You've now explained to us. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said you were on good terms first and then when you no longer did the job you did, there was no need to have any contact with him. That's about it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me this, please: On page 50, you state the names of four individuals, Marko Pavlovic, Brane Grujic, Rade Peric, and Marinko Vasilic. Those are the names of the people. Who are they? Who are these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brane Grujic was the president of the municipality and Crisis Staff, the provisional government, in fact. Marko Pavlovic was the commander of the TO for a time. Marinko Vasilic was a man who was in the police force. He was my assistant. And afterwards, he performed other functions. He feels commander, chief, and so on. And Rade Peric for a time in 1992, up until February 1993, held the post of the president of the executive board of the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So these four men that you list, you list by virtue of their offices, the positions they occupied; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably in that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you this because I understood from what is written here that you treat them as individuals who had to have been informed with everything that went on and that they were possibly responsible for any crimes, if any crimes were committed, that that's how you referred to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, Mr. Milosevic. But when you -- only when we speak of the chief of police. In 1992, five or six people performed that function, held that post. So there was a lot of rotation, as happened with the other posts and positions as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But may I understand it in this way, that you enumerate these people as being the most high responsible, holding the most high responsible posts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they held top posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you don't actually link them to any crimes that were commit there had. You just name them as people who were in the top echelons, that held the main posts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is absolutely correct. I do not correct connect them to any events that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you were enumerating, you would have to include your name on that list too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At a given point in time, I held responsible posts and did mention myself during my testimony. At a certain point in time, I was TO commander, chief of police in Zvornik, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So what they knew, you had to know by virtue of office.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Up until the 20th of April, while I was in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's why I wanted to clear this point up. I don't know if any of these people will be coming into the court here, so I assume that the knowledge they had was knowledge you shared too, so that we can clarify certain points, I hope, in the most authentic way possible. So those -- that is my line of thinking, and I'm trying to clear all this up. You said that a division took place, and at one point you said that negotiations were held, and you mentioned negotiations in particular between the Muslims, Serbs, and Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember that? Do you remember having mentioned that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, these divisions which you planned and which you knew about --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What I understood was that they in fact followed on from what was being negotiated between the parties at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know - and I assume that you must know, because you held a high function - that those divisions were then in a way defined and specified by the Cutileiro Plan, signed by all three parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that the question was defined, that is to say, the position of Serbs in Bosnia was defined on the basis of that plan, and that a certain division had been agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right, I see. And you do know that all three sides signed the plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that after that Alija Izetbegovic withdrew his signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that too. I know that he said that the plan would not hold true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, as somebody who delved in politics in a way and occupied a high-ranking post, was it like this: Negotiations were held at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina, an agreement and plan was reached, and in conformity with that plan certain divisions are made, after that Izetbegovic withdraws his signature and the divisions remain? Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that after this plan was refuted by Izetbegovic, that the problems arose and the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina could no longer be controlled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And to follow on from that, the -- instead of agreement following on from that plan, what happened was conflict and clashes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. That's fine. I think we've clearly shown that to be the case. Now, tell me this - and I'm just going to quote you on this point here, and I'm sure you'll recall having said it. I made a note of it while you were testifying several days ago - you were talking about the distribution of weapons, the issuance of weapons. "The Crisis Staff issued and distributed weapons to Serb villages according to an assessment of the degree to which these villages were threatened." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can we then take it -- may we observe that these villages were in jeopardy, were threatened? Because your basic criteria for distributing weapons, according to what you yourself said, was your evaluation as to how far the Serb villages were threatened. So the villages were indeed threatened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information was that the Muslim side was arming itself. And you must understand our positions. In Zvornik we made up under 39 per cent of the population, and we felt ourselves to be under threat, security-wise and safety-wise. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But as far as I understand it from your explanations, in view of the different degree of jeopardy for the different villages, how far different villages were threatened, you evaluated the degree to which they were actually threatened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were Serb villages who were in a purely Muslim encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And I'm sure you had information as to how far the other side were arming themselves and how far the Patriotic League was being formed and armed in 1991. Did all these factors -- were all these factors taken into consideration when you evaluated how far a village was threatened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely how we did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I think you even said -- well, not to say "even said." I just want to focus on a detail in your testimony. When you distributed the weapons according to the degree to which villages were under threat - and we have established that they were indeed under threat - you said that you kept records; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And all the people that were issued weapons would sign for it; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So there was no random distribution of weapons or - how shall I put this - secret, clandestine activities. Everybody would sign for the weapon he received. And this -- the purpose of receiving weapons was to defend the villages under threat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the people would sign for it. All this was done according to -- in an organised fashion and planned fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Referring to the media, you said that there was a war in Croatia, the media were divided, each routed for its own side. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, as we're talking about your own region - and you know everything about that area, because you lived in it - was there anything on the subject of Zvornik which was published by the media that was false in any way, a lie in any way? Did the media publish any lies about Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You even said that Zvornik wasn't -- that the media didn't focus on Zvornik at all until the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's right. I don't think the media paid any attention to Zvornik until the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I should now like you to assist me, to help me clarify a particular point. It is exhibit -- the exhibit that was presented here. It is Exhibit -- and it is linked to the meeting -- it refers to the meeting you spoke about of the SDS in Sarajevo, at the Holiday Inn hotel on the 19th and 20th of December, 1991. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I attended that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have Exhibit 434, tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Have you found it? You have. All right. Fine. At the meeting, the entire leadership of the SDS attended.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood it, you were given these instructions pertaining to the organisation and activities of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina under extraordinary situations, in an emergency situation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was distributed to the leaders of the board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The SDS being the Serbian Democratic Party; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in tab 4 we have the conclusions. So you were at the meeting on the 19th and 20th of December held at the Holiday Inn hotel. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And already on the 22nd of December, as it says in this document, in tab 4, "The Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia-Herzegovina, municipal board of Zvornik," that's what it says, you make the following conclusions, conclusions by which you implement the instructions given you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's have a look at all this. As these instructions, this set of instructions, are in exhibit here, and they were presented a number of times and referred to a number of times, without - how shall I put it - without entering into its contents, actually, into the substance of the document itself. There is reference to Variant B -- Variant A and Variant B. And as you were absent for a few days, this gave me time to read through the document from start to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we'd better return to this after the adjournment. It's now time to take the break. We'll adjourn now, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you have if you want it an hour and a quarter more with this witness, if you require it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Witness B-024, tell me, please, since you certainly read very carefully those instructions even then: As far as I'm able to see, reading through it, there's virtually no difference between what it says for Variant A and for Variant B. Most of the points are repeated in both versions, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. The Variant B was envisaged for municipalities in which the Serbs were in a minority. And in Variant A, the Serbs already had power; whereas, in Variant B they didn't have power because they were in the minority. That is the major difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That is the point. But let us go back to the territory of the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In those days, the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina was mostly in the hands of these three national parties, the SDA, the SDS, and the HDZ. And representatives of the SDS had a little over one-third of deputy seats; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina was composed on a parity basis of Muslim, Serbs, and Croats; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
